name: /wtft
tagline: Where The F***ing Tokens?! (WTFT) - Cost Auditing Widget
description: Displays a horizontal, stacked TUI bar chart widget of your session's cost during each activity (Spec, Code, Plan, Agents, ...). Bars are cost totals tagged by each turn's action - every turn's cost includes the context re-send overhead regardless of category, and Prompt means pure conversational replies. For an input/output token decomposition use --tokens.

why.scenario: You just finished a coding session and want to see where your token costs went — was it all spec-writing or code refactoring?
why.result: A stacked bar chart widget appears showing your cost during each activity (Spec, Code, Plan, Agents, ...) over 1-hour intervals. You see exactly which hours cost the most.

why.scenario: You're tracking costs over a full workday and want finer granularity.
why.result: The last 12 four-hour intervals are displayed, giving you a two-day cost breakdown at quarter-day resolution.

why.scenario: You're auditing Claude Code sessions (not Pi) to compare costs across harnesses.
why.result: The chart pulls session data from your Claude Code session directory instead of Pi's, rendering the same bar chart for Claude interactions. (CLI only — the Pi extension auto-discovers Pi sessions.)

why.scenario: You're standing in a git worktree (or the main clone) and the session you want was recorded from a sibling checkout of the same repo — or from a worktree that has since been removed.
why.result: The session selector lists sessions from every checkout of the current repo, not just the exact directory you are standing in, and it works the same in both directions (clone sees worktrees, worktree sees clone). Worktree rows compact to <repo>/w/<branch> so they stay readable. A session whose directory was deleted is still found — from the moves the transcript itself records — and is shown under a directory that still exists. Outside a git repo nothing fans out. Use --dir <path> to anchor the fan-out somewhere other than the current directory.

why.scenario: You want to scroll through a long cost history that doesn't fit in the TUI widget.
why.result: A fullscreen scrollable pager overlay opens with the expanded cost timeline. (Pi TUI only — not available in the CLI.)

why.scenario: The 'Other' category in your WTFT widget is consuming a large share of your session cost and you want to drill into which specific commands are causing it.
why.result: A grouped histogram appears, breaking 'Other' commands into semantic sub-categories (Build & Bundling, Linting & Formatting, System Utilities, etc.) with per-command counts and costs. Unclassified commands appear under their own section.

why.scenario: You're running Claude Code and want a companion terminal showing live token costs as your session progresses.
why.result: A real-time updating bar chart renders in-place as new interactions are logged. Runs until Ctrl+C or 'q'. Scrollback above the chart is preserved. Ideal in a separate tmux pane.

why.scenario: You want to see the exact USD amount on your billing invoice or reconcile costs across multiple providers.
why.result: WTFT uses public pricing estimates per model and excludes things like caching discounts, free-tier credits, or provider-specific billing nuances. It's a directional cost-awareness tool — not an accounting ledger.

why.scenario: Your harness's own cost counter reads higher than WTFT's TOTAL and you want to know whether WTFT is miscounting or just can't see something.
why.result: TOTAL is strictly derived from recorded usage — every dollar traces to a `usage` object in the transcript. Below it, an UNCOUNTED line names the events the harness bills for but writes no usage for: /compact requests and 'while you were away' recaps, counted across the session and every subagent transcript. They are deliberately NOT priced and NOT in TOTAL. Measured across seven logged Claude Code sessions, this blind spot was 4.72% of the harness's own counter. The line appears only when a count is non-zero, and only in this non-watch --tokens path — --watch does not render it yet.
demo: Model           Input     Output  Reasoning Cache-Read Cache-Write       Cost
UNCOUNTED  3 recaps — billed by the harness; the transcript records
no usage for them, so they are NOT in TOTAL above (#149)

why.scenario: Your session has been idle for a while and the model cache has expired, or you're running a local model like Ollama with no remote caching at all.
why.result: Instead of hiding the widget or showing stale data, WTFT displays 'Cache Empty' (cloud models) or 'No Cache (local model)' in the widget area, plus the daemon's idle countdown. You know immediately whether the session is just idle or cache-free.

usage.desc: Group cost data into arbitrary binned intervals of minutes, hours, days, weeks, or turns (e.g., 1m, 7m, 4h, 1d, 2w, 5t; turn unit accepts t, turn, or turns; default: 1h).
Limit the number of interval bars displayed. Default: 100 in the CLI, 10 in the Pi extension.

Specify an explicit session .jsonl file path, or a fuzzy substring filter (e.g. 'b04c'). When the argument is not an existing file, it filters discovered sessions by basename or path substring. If exactly one match, runs immediately; if multiple, shows the session selector filtered to matching sessions. An absolute .jsonl path that does not exist YET is accepted as a pending session (#308), reported at exit 0 rather than as an error.

Anchor directory for Claude Code session discovery (default: current directory). The flag picks the anchor, not the policy: when the anchor sits inside a git repo, discovery fans out over every checkout of that repo (main clone plus every worktree), so sibling-worktree sessions are listed too. An anchor outside any git repo means exactly that directory, so '--dir ~' still does not list every session on the machine.

Set the maximum character width of the widget (default: 80). Pi extension only — the CLI parses the flag and ignores it, sizing output from the terminal width minus --pad. With no explicit width the extension sizes to the terminal and caps at 240; 240 is that cap, not a default.
Set the display timezone (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo) to avoid UTC display on servers (default: system local).
Render mode. --cumulative (default) shows running sums over time; --bucket shows discrete interval cost buckets.
Enable (default) or disable the proportional cost scale tick marks above the bars.
Launch an interactive scrollable fullscreen pager overlay to view expanded cost history. Pi TUI only — the CLI refuses -p with exit 1 and suggests piping to a pager instead.

Print a histogram of 'Other' commands grouped by semantic sub-category (Build, Lint, Test, Text & File Processing, System, etc.) with per-command counts and costs. A token that is not a plausible command name is normalizer residue, not a program that ran: those are quarantined under [Parse miss] and carry a ##PARSE-MISS## marker so misses can be counted rather than mistaken for commands. Tokens come from commands the session ran, so they are control-character-stripped and length-capped before rendering.

Show (default) or hide the WTFT cost-auditing widget below the editor. Pi extension only; both are accepted and inert in the CLI. -S carries no force of its own even in the extension: --hide --show and --show --hide both clear the widget.

Enable or disable emoji icons in the widget AND in CLI output, including watch mode. When disabled, clean single-width ASCII characters are used instead. Overrides the persisted setting for that run only.
Watch a session file for changes and re-render the bar chart in real-time (companion terminal mode for Claude Code). Ctrl+C to exit.
List all running log parser daemons with session path, PID, parser version, and idle time.
Kill log parser daemons whose source session no longer exists.
Kill all running log parser daemons (fresh spawn on next wtft).
Stop the log parser daemon for a specific session path.
Kill the log parser daemon, delete tag files, and force a full session re-parse.
Target a specific harness for auto-discovery (pi, claude-code, or auto). Default: auto.
Thinking token budget for utilization percentage display in --tokens output.

Emit one JSON object on stdout (schema wtft/session@2) instead of the chart: exact un-abbreviated totals, per-model rows with a 'priced' flag, per-category rows in a fixed order, the #149 uncounted blind spot, the #116 spawned lineage (with spawned.ledgerError saying the ledger could not be READ, which is not the same as nothing having spawned) plus a tree total, the provisional verdict as a field, and the session identity. total means THIS SESSION'S OWN TURNS; tree is total plus every RESOLVED launcher-spawned descendant the ledger records, so it is a floor whenever anything went uncounted -- unattributed, past the depth cap, or unreachable because the ledger could not be read, which spawned.ledgerError reports; the walk stops at depth 5, reported in the document, and a ledger over 8 MiB is refused outright rather than partly read. No ANSI and nothing else on stdout; human prose goes to stderr and the sentences that would otherwise have been stdout are repeated in the object's notices[]. Exit 9 still applies (see Exit codes). Suppresses the rendering flags (--tokens, --other, --pad, --interval, --limit, --bucket/--cumulative, --ticks, --emoji, --timezone). Does NOT apply to the commands that run instead of a report: --help/--why/--version, --watch, and --list/--cleanup/--restart/--stop all keep their own output, and -p is still refused with exit 1. With several sessions discovered and no -s, --json does not prompt: it takes the newest and says so in notices[]. CLI only. See docs/spec-26-json.md.

Switch between token-unit mode and cost-unit mode ($). --tokens shows a per-model token summary table with utilization, plus — when the session or any of its subagent transcripts contains them — an UNCOUNTED line naming compactions and away-recaps (the same counts --json reports as `uncounted`, which it scans on every run): calls the harness bills for but writes no usage record for, so they are deliberately NOT in TOTAL (#149). --cost switches back to $ mode. Config-persistable.

Alias of --tokens: per-model token+cost breakdown table. Unpriced models (no registry entry and no legacy rate branch) are marked '?', and a legend names, per model, the fallback wtft would price it with. Extend the registry without a rebuild via ~/.config/princess-pi-tools/wtft-pricing.json.
Pad output with N spaces on each side (default: 1, max: floor(term/2)-1). Makes CLI output width match Pi TUI widget.
Display this help information.
Display this tool's version.
Explain why you'd run this tool, with user scenarios and anti-use-cases.

SUBCOMMAND, not a report (#116), and POSITIONAL -- it must be the first argument, so `wtft --json spawn-record ...` is a report run rather than a recording. Record one parent->child spawn edge in the append-only spawn ledger at $XDG_STATE_HOME/wtft/spawns.jsonl (~/.local/state/wtft/spawns.jsonl by default). A launcher-spawned session -- a pr-review lens, a `herdr agent start` child -- leaves NO trace of its parent in either session file, so there is nothing for a later parse to re-derive; the spawner writes the edge down at spawn time, when it is free, and `claude --session-id <uuid>` means the child's id is known before the child runs. --flag value and --flag=value both work. --json echoes the exact line written; without it nothing is printed. There is no --ts: the clock fills it, so the ledger cannot disagree with itself. Every text field is capped at 512 bytes and the whole line at 4 KiB, which is what keeps one record one write(2). Exits 2 on a missing or unknown flag, a flag with no value, a malformed session id, or an oversized field; 3 when the ledger cannot be written; 0 on a successful append and on --help. A spawner is expected to ignore a failure, since an unrecorded edge degrades to exactly the old behaviour. wtft --json then reports the lineage under `spawned`, with `tree` as self + resolved descendants; `total` keeps meaning this session's own turns.

exitCodes.meaning: Report produced — including when there is nothing to report yet (session file not written, or a tag with no classified data). Under --json the report is one JSON object on stdout; the commands that run instead of a report (--help/--why/--version, --list/--cleanup/--restart/--stop, and spawn-record on a successful append or --help) also exit 0 and print their own output.

Error: no session found or selected, an invalid path, a daemon that could not be spawned or that died before producing data, a refused flag (-p), or an unhandled exception. Reason on stderr; under --json stdout carries nothing.

`wtft spawn-record` only (#116): the call was wrong -- a missing required flag, an unknown flag, a flag with no value, a malformed session id, or an oversized field. Nothing was appended. The report path never exits 2.

`wtft spawn-record` only (#116): the record was valid but the ledger could not be written -- an unwritable state dir, or a full disk. The edge is NOT recorded, so the child is invisible to the rollup, not `unattributed` (which means an edge we have whose child we could not read). Any partial line left behind is reported as a counted malformed line on the next read; nothing tries to repair it.

Provisional (#443): the report was produced in full, but the total may still grow under the daemon. Under --json, provisional.provisional is true and provisional.reason names the condition, so $? and the field always agree. One condition is mode-dependent: subagent-unreadable is found by the uncounted scan, which runs under --tokens and --json but not on a plain wtft run, so a session provisional for that reason alone exits 9 in those two modes and 0 on a plain run (docs/spec-26-json.md, Exit codes).
The interactive session selector was cancelled with q or Ctrl-C. SIGINT convention (128+2), not a wtft-specific code. --json never prompts, so it never returns this.
